title: User API errors during morning peak
executive_summary: INC-009: user endpoint errors began ~07:57-08:00Z. user-service error rate rose from ~0.4% to ~23%, and api-gateway error rate from ~0.5% to ~8%. The onset coincides with the user-service 7.2.0 deployment at 07:56Z, whose logged errors are NPEs in ProfileBatchLoader. Latency and resource metrics stayed flat. Likely cause: a regression in the 7.2.0 batch-loader change. Recommended action: roll back to 7.1.3.

hypotheses.description: The user-service 7.2.0 ORM-to-batch-loader change introduced a null-handling defect in ProfileBatchLoader.load, causing request failures that propagate as 500s through api-gateway. Mechanism: After the deployment at 07:56Z, ProfileBatchLoader throws NullPointerException on some requests and returns 500s. api-gateway records 5xx for GET /v1/users/*. Error rate jumps from ~0.4% to ~23% with flat latency and DB utilisation, consistent with fast-failing exceptions rather than saturation.

conclusion: The user API error spike began at 07:57-08:00Z, within about a minute of the user-service v7.2.0 deployment (dep-c02e51b7 at 07:56Z, "Switch ORM to batch loader"). The errors are NullPointerExceptions in ProfileBatchLoader.load, and api-gateway 5xx responses from user-service follow. Latency, DB connection utilisation, CPU, timeouts and request rate stayed at baseline, so this looks like a code-level failure rather than capacity exhaustion. Rolling back user-service to 7.1.3 is the recommended mitigation; confirmation is pending a post-rollback recovery check.
